newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends lower on feed supplies, Dow drop.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends lower on feed supplies, Dow drop.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed lower on persistent reminders of a buildup in feed supplies with a drop in the Dow industrials early Tuesday also viewed as unnerving to potential longs, traders said.

The Dow fell 50 points early, triggering index-arbitrage trading curbs on the New York Stock Exchange, before recouping a portion of the early losses. At 1518 CST the index traded at 6528.41, down 19.38 points.
A drop in the wheat market also was noted.
"This market is going nowhere for awhile, there's too much feed around," a trader said.
Corn rallied early Monday on bullish input from USDA's Cattle-on-Feed Report and on a greater-than-expected number for corn in USDA's weekly export inspections report.

But corn faltered as the December reached a session high of $2.77-1/2 a bushel Monday, just above technical resistance at $2.75-1/2. Support in the December Tuesday was first at $2.73 and second at $2.69-1/2.
Corn closed 1/2 to 2-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with December down 1-1/2 at $2.73-1/4. March closed 1/2 lower at $2.74-1/4.
Position squaring was featured before Friday, first notice day for deliveries on the December contract. Traders said deliveries are expected to be light. December Wednesday will trade without limits.
Volume was thin before the U.S. Thanksgiving Day Holiday on Thursday. CBOT grain futures markets will be closed Thursday and will close early Wednesday and Friday at 1210 CST/1810 GMT.
ADM Investor Services bought one million bushels of March and Prudential Securities bought two million bushels of March, traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated at 62,000 contracts, below the 84,445 traded Monday, according to the CBOT.
In corn options, LIT America sold 500 March $2.70 puts at seven cents, Iowa Grain bought 1,350 May $2.90 puts at 20 to 20-3/4 cents and Smith Barney sold 400 March $2.70 puts at 7-1/4 to 7-3/4 cents.
Corn options volume was estimated at 18,000 contracts, about the same as the 18,198 traded Monday.
